text:
Ottawa and Los Angeles both arrive stinging. The Senators lost 4-1 at Vegas two days ago and are 2-3-0 in their last five without Warren Foegele and William Eklund. The Kings fell 2-1 in Chicago, which snapped the Blackhawks' three-game winless run, and they're missing Mats Zuccarello and Alex Turcotte. With Zuccarello out, Joel Armia has moved beside Haula and Laferriere and is up to 15:32 a night from 13:08.

Our numbers see a close game, with Ottawa at 3.09 expected goals (the quality of chances created) and Los Angeles at 2.72. Both have been outchanced at five on five, Ottawa taking 50% of the expected goals and the Kings 48%. Ottawa's penalty problem stands out, 4.8 minors a game, though its power play (0.81 expected goals a game) is well ahead of the Kings' (0.54). In net, projected starter Jonas Johansson is at +1.0 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots should have allowed) over two games, after -10.72 last season. Darcy Kuemper, projected for Los Angeles, is at -1.39 this season and -6.77 last.

Tim Stützle is our top scoring pick, with a 35% chance to score and a 75% chance of a point. Drake Batherson, 63% to point, just had a hat trick that Yahoo Sports called one of the most improbable in Senators history. For the Kings, we like Artemi Panarin (70% to point) and Adrian Kempe (34% to score), a first-round pick in 2014 from Sweden's MODO.
